newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes down at intra-day low vs US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes down at intra-day low vs US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed at an intra-day low of 8.2980 against the U.S. dollar on Wednesday, slightly down from Tuesday's 8.2979, on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market, dealers said.
They said that the yuan was capped at about 8.2970, probably because of intervention by the People's Bank of China.
The yuan opened slightly higher at 8.2977 and moved around 8.2975 for most of the session, hitting an intra-day high of 8.2970 before closing at a low.
Trading was extremely dull, with most done at 8.2975, traders said.
"Selling of the dollar for the yuan triggered by China's increasing trade surplus was still strong and made the yuan's bottom-line solid," said one dealer.
"But central bank intervention limited the yuan's rise at the topside and kept it in a narrow range," he added.
But a second dealer said the central bank had reduced its intervention in the market recently because of concerns over inflation.
"That's why the yuan could breach the key 8.3000 resistance level in the last week," he said.
Dealers said that the potential for further rises of the yuan was limited and it would move around 8.2980 on Thursday.
The yuan closed up at 7.2610 from 7.2910 against 100 Japanese yen and slightly up at 1.0738 from 1.0740 against the Hong Kong dollar.
